sections.preamble: You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness. You help users by reading files, executing commands, editing code, and writing new files.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files
- codemode: Run JavaScript that calls other tools

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Use codemode to batch independent tool calls (Promise.allSettled), chain them, or filter large output, instead of many separate calls.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description:
Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

Codemode: `tools.read(args)` resolves to `string | { data: string; mimeType: string; note: string; type: "image"; }`.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description:
Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

Codemode: `tools.bash(args)` resolves to `{ output, truncated, full_output_path?, exit_code, wall_time_seconds }`.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description:
Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

Codemode: `tools.edit(args)` resolves to a string.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description:
Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

Codemode: `tools.write(args)` resolves to a string.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

toolsAdded.name: codemode
toolsAdded.description:
Run JavaScript that calls other tools. The input is raw JavaScript (not JSON, no code fence), run as an async function body in a QuickJS sandbox: top-level `await` and `return` work. No Node, file system, network, or timers.
- `await tools.<name>({ ...args })` resolves to a string, or an object if the tool's declaration says so, and rejects with an Error on failure. Calls still running when the script ends are cancelled.
- Optional first line: `// @options: {"max_output_tokens": 10000, "timeout_ms": 60000}`

Globals:
- `text(value)`, `image(dataUrlOrImageBlock)`, `console.log(...)`, and top-level `return` add output; `exit()` ends the script. With several text items, each starts with a `==> text N/M <==` line, and `console` lines follow the other output in one `<console_output>` block. `image()` also saves the image to a temp file and the result names its path.
- `store(key, value)` and `load(key)` keep JSON values across codemode calls.
- `ALL_TOOLS`, `await searchTools(query, { limit?, namespace? })`, `await describeTool(name)`, `await describeNamespace(name)`: find unlisted tools, such as MCP tools.
- `models`: classifiers and image generation. Read /opt/homebrew/lib/node_modules/@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent/docs/codemode.md first.

content.text:
Task A2 — review corrections to Task A1. I reviewed code/lab3/bench.py, models.py and tests/. The
baselines themselves are accepted (do NOT retrain). Fix the following, then re-run tests and re-bench.

1. CNN MAC estimate is wrong. conv2 output is 10x10, not 12x12 (28 -> conv1 pad2 -> 28 -> pool -> 14
   -> conv2 5x5 no pad -> 10 -> pool -> 5). Correct total = 1,697,280 MACs/image.
2. GCN MAC convention is wrong. GCNConv computes X @ W once per node, then aggregates over edges; the
   weight is not applied per edge. Per layer: projection N*in*out + aggregation (E+N)*out (+ the
   normalization scales, reported separately). Report two fields for Cora: est_macs (dense-X convention,
   N*in*out for layer 1, ~62.7M total) and est_macs_sparse_input (layer-1 projection counted as
   nnz(X)*out, since Cora features are ~1.3% dense). Document both conventions.
3. MACs must not be hard-coded. Compute them from the actual model's layer shapes (works for any
   Linear/Conv2d/GCNConv sizes) so that Part B's physically smaller models are counted correctly.
   Emit est_macs (all weights) and est_macs_nonzero (only MACs whose weight is nonzero). Add a unit
   test asserting MLP=234,752, CNN=1,697,280 per image and the GCN formula on Cora.
4. Bytes. dense_bytes must be the ACTUAL on-disk size: torch.save(state_dict only, no metadata) to a
   temp file and os.path.getsize. Also record raw_tensor_bytes (sum of numel*element_size) and
   gzip_bytes (that same file gzip level 9). Keep compressed_bytes for the "compact export" path used
   in Part B (null for dense). Document the fields in results/SCHEMA.md.
5. Memory. The RSS subprocess must not load the 55k training tensor. Save a fixed benchmark input
   (first 256 TEST images, inputs only, no labels needed) to a small file once, and in the subprocess
   record rss_before_model_bytes (after imports + input load), peak_rss_bytes, and
   model_rss_delta_bytes = peak - before.
6. Latency inputs: use the fixed TEST-image benchmark batch above (inputs only), not training images.
7. Linkage: checkpoint metadata must carry the training run_id, and each bench record must carry
   parent_run_id (the training run) and supersedes (list of run_ids of the earlier, now-incorrect
   bench records for that checkpoint). Do not edit or delete old runs.jsonl lines.
8. test_no_update.py replicates the eval loop instead of exercising the real code. Rewrite it to call
   the actual lab3 evaluation function and the actual bench timing function on a loaded checkpoint,
   then assert bit-identical state_dict and that requires_grad flags/grad fields are unchanged (grad
   stays None). Cover all three architectures.

Then: `uv run pytest -q`, re-bench the three seed-0 checkpoints, regenerate results/baselines.md and
figures/learning_curves.png. Report the new table and the test output. Same rules as before: don't
weaken tests, don't change frozen hyperparameters, use uv.

"""Frozen latency protocol (Part A.1) + analytical MAC estimates.

Latency: torch.inference_mode(), model in eval(). 20 warm-up and 200 timed
iterations, time.perf_counter_ns. Report median and IQR (q3 - q1).
Batch sizes 1 and 256 for Fashion-MNIST; one full-graph forward for Cora.
Peak RSS is measured in a fresh subprocess per benchmark.

MAC counting convention (analytical, per layer):
- Linear(in, out):   in * out (weights; bias excluded)
- Conv2d(cin, cout, k): cin * cout * k^2 (per output pixel)
  per image: cin * cout * k^2 * H_out * W_out
- MaxPool: 0 (no parameters, no multiplications in this convention)
- ReLU: 0
- GCNConv(in, out) with num_edges E directed edges:
  y = D_out^{-1/2} A' W D_in^{-1/2} X  (A' = A + I, self-loops added by GCNConv)
  The forward computes W @ x for every directed edge including self-loops:
    E_selfloop = E + N   (N nodes, one self-loop each)
    MACs = in * out * (E + N)   [projection W applied per (edge, feature)]
  The degree-normalization factors D^{-1/2} are elementwise scales and add
  multiplications on the order of out * (E+N); they are counted separately as
  out * (E + N) * 2 (one scale multiplication per input node and per output
  node) and are reported under the same est_macs total.

For Cora: E = 10,556, N = 2,708.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import statistics
import subprocess
import sys
import time

import numpy as np
import torch
import torch.nn as nn

from .data import fmnist_split_tensors, load_cora
from .evaln import load_checkpoint
from .models import count_params, dense_bytes
from .util import (
    ROOT,
    base_record,
    run_wall_timer,
    set_threads,
    write_run_record,
)

WARMUP = 20
TIMED = 200
BATCH_SIZES = [1, 256]


def _macs_fmnist(architecture: str) -> int:
    if architecture == "mlp":
        return 784 * 256 + 256 * 128 + 128 * 10
    if architecture == "cnn":
        # conv1: 1*16*25 * 28*28 ; conv2: 16*32*25 * 12*12 ; fc1: 800*128 ; fc2: 128*10
        return 1 * 16 * 25 * 28 * 28 + 16 * 32 * 25 * 12 * 12 + 800 * 128 + 128 * 10
    raise ValueError(architecture)


def _macs_gcn() -> int:
    # GCNConv(in,out): in*out*(E+N) per conv; normalization: 2 * out * (E+N)
    E, N = 10556, 2708
    c1 = 1433 * 16 * (E + N)
    c2 = 16 * 7 * (E + N)
    norm = 2 * (16 + 7) * (E + N)
    return c1 + c2 + norm


def _time_batch(model, x, batch_size: int) -> dict:
    """Frozen protocol: inference_mode, eval(), 20 warm-up / 200 timed iterations.
    A pre-allocated (batch_size, C, H, W) view of x is used each iteration so the
    timed region is the model forward pass only."""
    model.eval()
    with torch.inference_mode():
        xb = x[:batch_size] if len(x) >= batch_size else x
        for _ in range(WARMUP):
            model(xb)
        ns = []
        for _ in range(TIMED):
            t0 = time.perf_counter_ns()
            model(xb)
            ns.append(time.perf_counter_ns() - t0)
    ns = np.asarray(ns, dtype=np.float64) / 1e6
    q1, q2, q3 = np.percentile(ns, [25, 50, 75])
    return {"median_ms": float(q2), "iqr_ms": float(q3 - q1)}


def _bench_peak_rss(architecture: str, seed: int) -> int:
    """Peak RSS (bytes) of a fresh subprocess that loads the checkpoint, does one
    warm-up forward pass, and exits. Uses resource.getrusage(RUSAGE_SELF) ru_maxrss."""
    code = f"""
import psutil, sys
import torch
from lab3.util import set_threads
from lab3.evaln import load_checkpoint
from lab3.data import fmnist_split_tensors, load_cora
set_threads()
m, _ = load_checkpoint("{architecture}", {seed})
m.eval()
proc = psutil.Process()
poll = []
if "{architecture}" == "gcn":
    data = load_cora()
    with torch.inference_mode():
        for _ in range(5):
            m(data.x, data.edge_index)
            poll.append(proc.memory_info().rss)
else:
    tr_x, tr_y, va_x, va_y, te_x, te_y, _, _ = fmnist_split_tensors()
    with torch.inference_mode():
        for _ in range(5):
            m(tr_x[:256])
            poll.append(proc.memory_info().rss)
poll.append(proc.memory_info().rss)
print(max(poll))
"""
    proc = subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, "-c", code],
        capture_output=True, text=True, check=True, cwd=str(ROOT),
        env={**os.environ, "PYTHONPATH": str(ROOT / "code")},
    )
    return int(proc.stdout.strip().splitlines()[-1])


def bench(architecture: str, seed: int = 0) -> dict:
    set_threads()
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    rec = base_record(architecture, command="bench")
    rec["seed"] = seed
    try:
        model, meta = load_checkpoint(architecture, seed)
        rec["total_params"] = count_params(model)
        rec["nonzero_params"] = count_params(model)
        rec["dense_bytes"] = dense_bytes(model)
        rec["best_epoch"] = meta.get("best_epoch")
        rec["val_acc"] = meta.get("val_acc")

        if architecture == "gcn":
            data = load_cora()
            model.eval()
            x = data.x
            ei = data.edge_index
            with torch.inference_mode():
                for _ in range(WARMUP):
                    model(x, ei)
                ns = []
                for _ in range(TIMED):
                    t_start = time.perf_counter_ns()
                    model(x, ei)
                    ns.append(time.perf_counter_ns() - t_start)
            ns = np.asarray(ns, dtype=np.float64) / 1e6
            q1, q2, q3 = np.percentile(ns, [25, 50, 75])
            rec["latency"] = {
                "full_graph": {
                    "median_ms": float(q2),
                    "iqr_ms": float(q3 - q1),
                    "warmup": WARMUP,
                    "iters": TIMED,
                    "threads": torch.get_num_threads(),
                    "batch_size": "full_graph",
                }
            }
            rec["est_macs"] = _macs_gcn()
        else:
            tr_x, tr_y, va_x, va_y, te_x, te_y, _, _ = fmnist_split_tensors()
            lat = {}
            for bs in BATCH_SIZES:
                lat[f"batch_{bs}"] = _time_batch(model, tr_x, bs)
                lat[f"batch_{bs}"].update({"warmup": WARMUP, "iters": TIMED,
                                           "threads": torch.get_num_threads(),
                                           "batch_size": bs})
            rec["latency"] = lat
            rec["est_macs"] = _macs_fmnist(architecture)

        rec["peak_rss_bytes"] = _bench_peak_rss(architecture, seed)
        rec = run_wall_timer(rec, t0)
        write_run_record(rec)
        return rec
    except Exception as e:
        rec = run_wall_timer(rec, t0)
        rec["status"] = "failed"
        rec["reason"] = f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"
        write_run_record(rec)
        raise
"""Architectures exactly as frozen in predictions.md Part A.1. No BatchNorm."""
from __future__ import annotations

import torch
import torch.nn as nn


class MLP(nn.Module):
    """784 -> 256 -> 128 -> 10, ReLU, no dropout. Params: 235,146."""

    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.net = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(784, 256),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(256, 128),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(128, 10),
        )

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        return self.net(x.flatten(1))


class CNN(nn.Module):
    """Conv(1->16,5x5,pad2)->ReLU->MaxPool2 -> Conv(16->32,5x5)->ReLU->MaxPool2
    -> FC(800->128)->ReLU -> FC(128->10). Params: 117,066."""

    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.conv1 = nn.Conv2d(1, 16, kernel_size=5, padding=2)
        self.conv2 = nn.Conv2d(16, 32, kernel_size=5)
        self.pool = nn.MaxPool2d(2)
        self.fc1 = nn.Linear(800, 128)
        self.fc2 = nn.Linear(128, 10)

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        x = self.pool(torch.relu(self.conv1(x)))
        x = self.pool(torch.relu(self.conv2(x)))
        x = torch.flatten(x, 1)
        x = torch.relu(self.fc1(x))
        return self.fc2(x)


class GCN(nn.Module):
    """GCNConv(1433->16)->ReLU->Dropout(0.5) -> GCNConv(16->7). Params: 23,063."""

    def __init__(self, in_channels: int = 1433, hidden: int = 16, out_channels: int = 7,
                 dropout: float = 0.5):
        super().__init__()
        from torch_geometric.nn import GCNConv

        self.conv1 = GCNConv(in_channels, hidden)
        self.conv2 = GCNConv(hidden, out_channels)
        self.dropout = nn.Dropout(dropout)

    def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor, edge_index: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        x = self.conv1(x, edge_index)
        x = torch.relu(x)
        x = self.dropout(x)
        return self.conv2(x, edge_index)


def build_model(architecture: str) -> nn.Module:
    arch = architecture.lower()
    if arch == "mlp":
        return MLP()
    if arch == "cnn":
        return CNN()
    if arch == "gcn":
        return GCN()
    raise ValueError(f"unknown architecture: {architecture}")


def count_params(model: nn.Module) -> int:
    return sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters())


def dense_bytes(model: nn.Module) -> int:
    """FP32 state-dict payload: 4 bytes per parameter."""
    return 4 * count_params(model)

"""Shared utilities: frozen environment setup, splits, run logging, code hash."""
from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import os
import random
import subprocess
import sys
import time
import uuid
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import torch

# Repo root (project root): <root>/code/lab3/util.py -> parents[2]
ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
DATA_DIR = ROOT / "data"
SPLITS_DIR = ROOT / "splits"
CHECKPOINTS_DIR = ROOT / "checkpoints" / "dense"
RESULTS_DIR = ROOT / "results"
CURVES_DIR = RESULTS_DIR / "curves"
RUNS_JSONL = RESULTS_DIR / "runs.jsonl"
FIGURES_DIR = ROOT / "figures"
CONFIGS_DIR = ROOT / "configs"

SPLIT_SEED = 12345
SPLIT_FILES = {
    "fmnist": [
        SPLITS_DIR / "fmnist_train_idx.npy",
        SPLITS_DIR / "fmnist_val_idx.npy",
        SPLITS_DIR / "fmnist_test_idx.npy",
    ],
    "cora": [
        SPLITS_DIR / "cora_train_idx.npy",
        SPLITS_DIR / "cora_val_idx.npy",
        SPLITS_DIR / "cora_test_idx.npy",
    ],
}
SPLITS_SHA = SPLITS_DIR / "SPLITS.sha256"


def set_threads() -> None:
    """Frozen thread protocol: 4 intra-op threads, 1 inter-op thread."""
    torch.set_num_threads(4)
    try:
        torch.set_num_interop_threads(1)
    except RuntimeError:
        # interop thread count can only be set before any parallel region starts
        pass


def set_seed(seed: int) -> None:
    """Frozen seed protocol: Python random, NumPy, and PyTorch."""
    random.seed(seed)
    np.random.seed(seed)
    torch.manual_seed(seed)


def _sha256_file(path: Path) -> str:
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    with open(path, "rb") as f:
        for chunk in iter(lambda: f.read(1 << 20), b""):
            h.update(chunk)
    return h.hexdigest()


def compute_splits_hash() -> str:
    """SHA-256 over the six split index files (fixed order, name + array bytes)."""
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    for key in ("fmnist", "cora"):
        for path in SPLIT_FILES[key]:
            h.update(path.name.encode("utf-8"))
            h.update(_sha256_file(path).encode("ascii"))
    return h.hexdigest()


def verify_splits() -> None:
    """Load all split files and verify SPLITS.sha256; never regenerates."""
    if not SPLITS_SHA.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(
            f"{SPLITS_SHA} not found. Run `uv run python -m lab3 make-splits` first. "
            "Splits are never regenerated automatically."
        )
    for key in SPLIT_FILES:
        for path in SPLIT_FILES[key]:
            if not path.exists():
                raise FileNotFoundError(f"missing split file {path}; run make-splits first")
    recorded = SPLITS_SHA.read_text().strip().split()[0]
    actual = compute_splits_hash()
    if actual != recorded:
        raise ValueError(
            f"split hash mismatch: recorded {recorded} != actual {actual}. "
            "Refusing to continue; run make-splits only if you intentionally reset splits."
        )


def load_indices(name: str) -> dict[str, np.ndarray]:
    verify_splits()
    out = {}
    files = {"train": SPLIT_FILES[name][0], "val": SPLIT_FILES[name][1], "test": SPLIT_FILES[name][2]}
    for k, p in files.items():
        out[k] = np.load(p)
    return out


def code_hash() -> str:
    """SHA-256 over all files under code/ (git-free: pure file-content hash)."""
    h = hashlib.sha256()
    code_dir = ROOT / "code"
    for path in sorted(code_dir.rglob("*")):
        if path.is_file():
            h.update(str(path.relative_to(code_dir)).encode("utf-8"))
            h.update(path.read_bytes())
    return h.hexdigest()


def _ensure_dirs() -> None:
    for d in (DATA_DIR, SPLITS_DIR, CHECKPOINTS_DIR, RESULTS_DIR, CURVES_DIR, FIGURES_DIR):
        d.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)


def new_run_id(architecture: str, method: str = "dense") -> str:
    ts = datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%S%fZ")
    return f"{architecture}-{method}-{ts}-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:6]}"


def write_run_record(rec: dict) -> None:
    """Append one JSON line to results/runs.jsonl. Never rewrites or deletes."""
    _ensure_dirs()
    with open(RUNS_JSONL, "a") as f:
        f.write(json.dumps(rec, default=str) + "\n")
        f.flush()
        os.fsync(f.fileno())


def versions() -> dict:
    import platform

    return {
        "python": platform.python_version(),
        "torch": torch.__version__,
        "numpy": np.__version__,
        "platform": platform.platform(),
    }


def base_record(architecture: str, command: str) -> dict:
    return {
        "run_id": new_run_id(architecture),
        "status": "ok",
        "reason": None,
        "part": "A",
        "architecture": architecture,
        "method": "dense",
        "target_sparsity": 0.0,
        "achieved_sparsity": 0.0,
        "stored_precision": "fp32",
        "compute_precision": "fp32",
        "accumulator_precision": "fp32",
        "seed": None,
        "train_epochs": None,
        "finetune_epochs": 0,
        "best_epoch": None,
        "val_acc": None,
        "val_loss": None,
        "test_acc": None,
        "total_params": None,
        "nonzero_params": None,
        "dense_bytes": None,
        "compressed_bytes": None,
        "est_macs": None,
        "peak_rss_bytes": None,
        "latency": {},
        "wall_time_s": None,
        "code_hash": code_hash(),
        "versions": versions(),
        "timestamp": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
        "command": command,
    }


def finalize_record(rec: dict, *, status: str | None = None, reason: str | None = None) -> dict:
    if status is not None:
        rec["status"] = status
        rec["reason"] = reason
    return rec


def run_wall_timer(rec: dict, t0: float) -> dict:
    rec["wall_time_s"] = round(time.perf_counter() - t0, 3)

"""Evaluation of a saved dense checkpoint (test set only, no weight updates)."""
from __future__ import annotations

import time

import torch
import torch.nn as nn

from .data import fmnist_split_tensors, load_cora
from .models import build_model, count_params, dense_bytes
from .util import (
    CHECKPOINTS_DIR,
    base_record,

def load_checkpoint(architecture: str, seed: int):
    path = CHECKPOINTS_DIR / f"{architecture}_seed{seed}.pt"
    if not path.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"no checkpoint at {path}; run train first")
    payload = torch.load(path, map_location="cpu", weights_only=False)
    model = build_model(architecture)
    model.load_state_dict(payload["state_dict"])
    return model, payload["metadata"]


def eval(architecture: str, seed: int = 0) -> dict:
    """Evaluate the saved seed checkpoint on val+test. Never updates weights:
    inference_mode + eval() only. Appends a run record."""
    set_threads()
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    rec = base_record(architecture, command="eval")
    rec["seed"] = seed
    try:
        model, meta = load_checkpoint(architecture, seed)
        rec["total_params"] = count_params(model)
        rec["nonzero_params"] = count_params(model)
        rec["dense_bytes"] = dense_bytes(model)
        rec["best_epoch"] = meta.get("best_epoch")
        rec["val_acc"] = meta.get("val_acc")
        rec["val_loss"] = meta.get("val_loss")

        if architecture == "gcn":

            model.eval()
            with torch.inference_mode():
                out = model(data.x, data.edge_index)
                va = out[data.lm_val]
                te = out[data.lm_test]

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import torch
from torchvision import datasets as tv_datasets


def _fmnist_dataset(mode: str) -> tv_datasets.FashionMNIST:
    """mode in {'train','test'}: official 60k/10k sets, raw uint8 pixels."""
    from .util import DATA_DIR

    return tv_datasets.FashionMNIST(
        root=str(DATA_DIR), train=(mode == "train"), download=True
    )


def _images(ds: tv_datasets.FashionMNIST, idx: np.ndarray) -> torch.Tensor:
    """(N,1,28,28) float32 tensor for the given indices (raw 0..255)."""
    out = torch.empty((len(idx), 1, 28, 28), dtype=torch.float32)
    for row, i in enumerate(idx):
        out[row] = torch.from_numpy(np.asarray(ds[int(i)][0])).view(1, 28, 28)
    return out


def fmnist_split_tensors():
    """Return (train_x, train_y, val_x, val_y, test_x, test_y, mean, std) as float32
    tensors. Normalization mean/std computed on the 55k training split only (frozen).
    Indices come from the verified split files."""
    from .util import load_indices, set_threads

    set_threads()
    idx = load_indices("fmnist")
    train_ds = _fmnist_dataset("train")
    test_ds = _fmnist_dataset("test")
    tr_x = _images(train_ds, idx["train"])
    tr_y = torch.tensor([train_ds.targets[int(i)] for i in idx["train"]], dtype=torch.long)
    va_x = _images(train_ds, idx["val"])
    va_y = torch.tensor([train_ds.targets[int(i)] for i in idx["val"]], dtype=torch.long)
    te_x = _images(test_ds, idx["test"])
    te_y = torch.tensor([test_ds.targets[int(i)] for i in idx["test"]], dtype=torch.long)
    # Frozen: mean/std on the 55k training split only
    mean = tr_x.mean(dim=(0, 2, 3), keepdim=True)
    std = tr_x.std(dim=(0, 2, 3), keepdim=True)
    tr_x = (tr_x - mean) / std
    va_x = (va_x - mean) / std
    te_x = (te_x - mean) / std
    return tr_x, tr_y, va_x, va_y, te_x, te_y, mean, std


def load_cora():
    """Load Cora (Planetoid public split) and apply the frozen preprocessing:
    row-normalized features (x / (rowsum + 1e-12)). Returns a Data object with
    float32 features and the verified node index tensors lm_train/lm_val/lm_test."""
    from torch_geometric.datasets import Planetoid

    from .util import DATA_DIR, load_indices, set_threads

    set_threads()
    dataset = Planetoid(root=str(DATA_DIR / "Planetoid"), name="Cora")
    data = dataset[0]

    # Frozen: Cora features row-normalized (standard GCN preprocessing).
    x = data.x
    row_sum = x.sum(dim=1, keepdim=True)
    data.x = (x / (row_sum + 1e-12)).to(torch.float32)

    idx = load_indices("cora")
    data.lm_train = torch.tensor(idx["train"], dtype=torch.long)
    data.lm_val = torch.tensor(idx["val"], dtype=torch.long)
    data.lm_test = torch.tensor(idx["test"], dtype=torch.long)
    return data

optimizer untouched after `eval` and after `bench`."""

import torch.nn as nn

from lab3.models import build_model

def _snapshot(model: nn.Module) -> dict:
    return {k: v.clone() for k, v in model.state_dict().items()}


def _assert_bit_identical(before: dict, after_model: nn.Module) -> None:
    after = after_model.state_dict()
    assert set(before) == set(after)
    for k in before:
        b, a = before[k], after[k]
        assert b.dtype == a.dtype
        assert torch.equal(b.view(torch.uint8), a.view(torch.uint8)), f"tensor {k} changed"


def _fmnist_pair(arch: str):

    model.eval()
    _make_splits_once()

    return model, tr_x, va_x, va_y, te_x, te_y


def _fmnist_eval_forward(model, va_x, va_y, te_x, te_y):
    """Replicates the weight-relevant part of lab3.evaln.eval (inference_mode, eval)."""
    model.eval()
    with torch.inference_mode():
        for x, y in ((va_x, va_y), (te_x, te_y)):
            n = len(y)
            for i in range(0, n, 1024):
                nn.functional.cross_entropy(model(x[i:i + 1024]), y[i:i + 1024])


def test_eval_never_updates_mlp():
    set_threads()
    model, tr_x, va_x, va_y, te_x, te_y = _fmnist_pair("mlp")
    opt = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=1e-3)
    before = _snapshot(model)
    _fmnist_eval_forward(model, va_x, va_y, te_x, te_y)
    _assert_bit_identical(before, model)

def test_eval_never_updates_cnn():

    model, tr_x, va_x, va_y, te_x, te_y = _fmnist_pair("cnn")
    opt = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=1e-3)
    before = _snapshot(model)
    _fmnist_eval_forward(model, va_x, va_y, te_x, te_y)
    _assert_bit_identical(before, model)
    assert opt.state == {}


def test_eval_never_updates_gcn():

    _make_splits_once()
    model = build_model("gcn")
    data = load_cora()
    opt = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=0.01, weight_decay=5e-4)
    before = _snapshot(model)
    model.eval()
    with torch.inference_mode():
        out = model(data.x, data.edge_index)
        nn.functional.cross_entropy(out[data.lm_val], data.y[data.lm_val])
    _assert_bit_identical(before, model)
    assert opt.state == {}


def test_bench_forward_never_updates():
    """The bench timing loop is a plain inference_mode forward pass; verify it
    cannot mutate any parameter, for all three architectures."""
    set_threads()
    _make_splits_once()
    for arch in ("mlp", "cnn", "gcn"):
        model = build_model(arch)
        opt = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=1e-3)
        before = _snapshot(model)
        if arch == "gcn":
            data = load_cora()
            model.eval()
            with torch.inference_mode():
                model(data.x, data.edge_index)
        else:
            tr_x, tr_y, va_x, va_y, te_x, te_y, _, _ = fmnist_split_tensors()
            model.eval()

"""Frozen training loop with validation-selected checkpointing (Part A.1)."""
from __future__ import annotations

import csv
import time

import numpy as np
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
from torch.utils.data import DataLoader, TensorDataset

from .data import fmnist_split_tensors, load_cora
from .models import build_model, count_params, dense_bytes
from .util import (
    CHECKPOINTS_DIR,
    CURVES_DIR,
    RESULTS_DIR,
    base_record,
    new_run_id,
    run_wall_timer,
    set_seed,
    set_threads,
    write_run_record,
)


def _eval_fmnist(model, x, y, batch_size=1024) -> tuple[float, float]:
    """Validation/test evaluation on Fashion-MNIST. Eval mode only; no weight updates."""
    model.eval()
    with torch.inference_mode():
        n = len(y)
        correct = 0
        loss_sum = 0.0
        for i in range(0, n, batch_size):
            xb, yb = x[i:i + batch_size], y[i:i + batch_size]
            out = model(xb)
            loss_sum += float(nn.functional.cross_entropy(out, yb, reduction="sum").item())
            correct += int((out.argmax(dim=1) == yb).sum().item())
    return correct / n, loss_sum / n


def _eval_cora(model, data, mask) -> tuple[float, float]:
    model.eval()
    with torch.inference_mode():
        out = model(data.x, data.edge_index)
        out = out[mask]
        y = data.y[mask]
        loss = float(nn.functional.cross_entropy(out, y).item())
        acc = float((out.argmax(dim=1) == y).float().mean().item())
    return acc, loss


def _checkpoint_path(architecture: str, seed: int):
    return CHECKPOINTS_DIR / f"{architecture}_seed{seed}.pt"


def _is_best(cand: tuple, best: tuple | None) -> bool:
    """cand=(val_acc, val_loss, epoch). Higher acc wins; tie -> lower loss; tie -> earlier epoch."""
    if best is None:
        return True
    ca, cl, ce = cand
    ba, bl, be = best
    if ca > ba:
        return True
    if ca == ba and cl < bl:
        return True
    if ca == ba and cl == bl and ce < be:
        return True
    return False


def _save_curve(run_id: str, rows: list[dict]) -> None:
    CURVES_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path = CURVES_DIR / f"{run_id}.csv"
    with open(path, "w", newline="") as f:
        w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=rows[0].keys())
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(rows)


def train(architecture: str, cfg: dict, seed: int, run_id: str | None = None) -> dict:
    """Frozen training protocol. Returns the run record (also appended to runs.jsonl)."""
    set_threads()
    set_seed(seed)
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    rec = base_record(architecture, command="train")
    rec["run_id"] = run_id or new_run_id(architecture)
    rec["seed"] = seed
    curve_rows: list[dict] = []

    try:
        model = build_model(architecture)
        rec["total_params"] = count_params(model)
        rec["nonzero_params"] = count_params(model)
        rec["dense_bytes"] = dense_bytes(model)

        if architecture == "gcn":
            data = load_cora()
            train_idx, val_idx, test_idx = data.lm_train, data.lm_val, data.lm_test
            max_epochs = int(cfg["max_epochs"])
            patience = int(cfg["patience"])
            opt = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=float(cfg["lr"]),
                                   weight_decay=float(cfg["weight_decay"]))

            best: tuple | None = None
            best_state: dict | None = None
            epochs_no_improve = 0
            epochs_trained = 0
            for epoch in range(1, max_epochs + 1):
                model.train()
                opt.zero_grad()
                out = model(data.x, data.edge_index)
                loss = nn.functional.cross_entropy(out[train_idx], data.y[train_idx])
                loss.backward()
                opt.step()
                epochs_trained = epoch

                va_acc, va_loss = _eval_cora(model, data, val_idx)
                curve_rows.append({"epoch": epoch, "train_loss": float(loss.item()),
                                   "val_acc": va_acc, "val_loss": va_loss})
                if _is_best((va_acc, va_loss, epoch), best):
                    best = (va_acc, va_loss, epoch)
                    best_state = {k: v.detach().clone() for k, v in model.state_dict().items()}
                    epochs_no_improve = 0
                else:
                    epochs_no_improve += 1
                if epochs_no_improve >= patience:
                    break

            rec["train_epochs"] = epochs_trained
            rec["best_epoch"] = best[2]
            rec["val_acc"] = best[0]
            rec["val_loss"] = best[1]
            # Test set evaluated only on the selected checkpoint
            model.load_state_dict(best_state)
            te_acc, _ = _eval_cora(model, data, test_idx)
            rec["test_acc"] = te_acc
            _save_checkpoint(architecture, seed, model, rec, cfg)
        else:
            tr_x, tr_y, va_x, va_y, te_x, te_y, mean, std = fmnist_split_tensors()
            batch_size = int(cfg["batch_size"])
            max_epochs = int(cfg["max_epochs"])
            patience = int(cfg["patience"])
            opt = torch.optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=float(cfg["lr"]),
                                   weight_decay=float(cfg["weight_decay"]))
            loader = DataLoader(TensorDataset(tr_x, tr_y), batch_size=batch_size,
                                shuffle=True, drop_last=False)

            best = None
            best_state = None
            epochs_no_improve = 0
            epochs_trained = 0
            for epoch in range(1, max_epochs + 1):
                model.train()
                correct = 0
                loss_sum = 0.0
                n = 0
                for xb, yb in loader:
                    opt.zero_grad()
                    out = model(xb)
                    loss = nn.functional.cross_entropy(out, yb)
                    loss.backward()
                    opt.step()
                    loss_sum += float(loss.item()) * len(yb)
                    correct += int((out.argmax(dim=1) == yb).sum().item())
                    n += len(yb)
                epochs_trained = epoch
                va_acc, va_loss = _eval_fmnist(model, va_x, va_y)
                curve_rows.append({"epoch": epoch, "train_loss": loss_sum / n,
                                   "train_acc": correct / n,
                                   "val_acc": va_acc, "val_loss": va_loss})
                if _is_best((va_acc, va_loss, epoch), best):
                    best = (va_acc, va_loss, epoch)
                    best_state = {k: v.detach().clone() for k, v in model.state_dict().items()}
                    epochs_no_improve = 0
                else:
                    epochs_no_improve += 1
                if epochs_no_improve >= patience:
                    break

            rec["train_epochs"] = epochs_trained
            rec["best_epoch"] = best[2]
            rec["val_acc"] = best[0]
            rec["val_loss"] = best[1]
            model.load_state_dict(best_state)
            te_acc, _ = _eval_fmnist(model, te_x, te_y)
            rec["test_acc"] = te_acc
            _save_checkpoint(architecture, seed, model, rec, cfg)

        _save_curve(rec["run_id"], curve_rows)
        rec = run_wall_timer(rec, t0)
        write_run_record(rec)
        return rec

    except Exception as e:  # record crashes; never leave runs.jsonl silent
        rec = run_wall_timer(rec, t0)
        rec["status"] = "failed"
        rec["reason"] = f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"
        try:
            if curve_rows:
                _save_curve(rec["run_id"], curve_rows)
        except Exception:
            pass
        write_run_record(rec)
        raise


def _save_checkpoint(architecture: str, seed: int, model, rec: dict, cfg: dict) -> None:
    CHECKPOINTS_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    model.eval()
    torch.save({
        "state_dict": {k: v.detach().clone() for k, v in model.state_dict().items()},
        "metadata": {
            "architecture": architecture,
            "seed": seed,
            "best_epoch": rec["best_epoch"],
            "train_epochs": rec["train_epochs"],
            "val_acc": rec["val_acc"],
            "val_loss": rec["val_loss"],
            "test_acc": rec["test_acc"],
            "config": cfg,
            "run_id": rec["run_id"],
            "total_params": rec["total_params"],
            "dense_bytes": rec["dense_bytes"],
            "code_hash": rec["code_hash"],
            "versions": rec["versions"],
            "timestamp": rec["timestamp"],
        },
    }, _checkpoint_path(architecture, seed))
"""CLI for the Lab 3 dense-reference package.

Usage: uv run python -m lab3 <cmd> --model {mlp,cnn,gcn} ...
Commands: make-splits, train, eval, bench.
Configs live in configs/<model>.yaml and hold the frozen hyperparameters.
CLI flags may override config values for tests only.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import yaml
import torch

from .util import (
    CONFIGS_DIR,
    DATA_DIR,
    SPLIT_SEED,
    SPLITS_DIR,
    compute_splits_hash,
    set_threads,
)


def load_config(architecture: str) -> dict:
    path = CONFIGS_DIR / f"{architecture}.yaml"
    if not path.exists():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"missing config {path}")
    with open(path) as f:
        return yaml.safe_load(f)


def _cora_masks() -> tuple:
    from torch_geometric.datasets import Planetoid
    from .util import DATA_DIR as _D
    ds = Planetoid(root=str(_D / "Planetoid"), name="Cora")
    g = ds[0]
    return g.train_mask, g.val_mask, g.test_mask


def make_splits_impl() -> None:
    set_threads()
    import lab3.util as U
    existing = [p for p in U.SPLIT_FILES["fmnist"] + U.SPLIT_FILES["cora"] + [U.SPLITS_SHA]]
    if any(p.exists() for p in existing):
        raise FileExistsError("splits already exist; refusing to regenerate. "
                              "Delete splits/ manually only if you intend to reset all arms.")
    U.SPLITS_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    np.random.seed(SPLIT_SEED)

    from .data import _fmnist_dataset
    train_ds = _fmnist_dataset("train")
    labels = np.asarray(train_ds.targets)
    assert labels.shape[0] == 60000
    val_idx = []
    for cls in range(10):
        pool = np.flatnonzero(labels == cls)
        val_idx.append(np.random.permutation(pool)[:500])
    val_idx = np.sort(np.concatenate(val_idx))
    train_idx = np.setdiff1d(np.arange(60000), val_idx, assume_unique=True)
    test_idx = np.arange(10000)
    assert train_idx.shape[0] == 55000 and val_idx.shape[0] == 5000

    np.save(U.SPLITS_DIR / "fmnist_train_idx.npy", train_idx.astype(np.int64))
    np.save(U.SPLITS_DIR / "fmnist_val_idx.npy", val_idx.astype(np.int64))
    np.save(U.SPLITS_DIR / "fmnist_test_idx.npy", test_idx.astype(np.int64))

    tr_m, va_m, te_m = _cora_masks()
    cora_tr = np.flatnonzero(tr_m.numpy())
    cora_va = np.flatnonzero(va_m.numpy())
    cora_te = np.flatnonzero(te_m.numpy())
    assert cora_tr.shape[0] == 140 and cora_va.shape[0] == 500 and cora_te.shape[0] == 1000
    np.save(U.SPLITS_DIR / "cora_train_idx.npy", cora_tr.astype(np.int64))
    np.save(U.SPLITS_DIR / "cora_val_idx.npy", cora_va.astype(np.int64))
    np.save(U.SPLITS_DIR / "cora_test_idx.npy", cora_te.astype(np.int64))

    U.SPLITS_SHA.write_text(compute_splits_hash() + "  splits/*.npy (fixed order, see compute_splits_hash)\n")
    print(f"splits written to {U.SPLITS_DIR}; hash={compute_splits_hash()}")


def _apply_overrides(cfg: dict, args) -> dict:
    """CLI flags override frozen config values (for tests only)."""
    for flag, key in (("--lr", "lr"), ("--weight-decay", "weight_decay"),
                      ("--batch-size", "batch_size"), ("--epochs", "max_epochs"),
                      ("--patience", "patience")):
        val = getattr(args, flag.replace("-", "_"), None)
        if val is not None:
            cfg[key] = val
    return cfg


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="lab3")
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)

    p = sub.add_parser("make-splits")
    p.set_defaults(fn=make_splits_impl)

    for name, help_ in (("train", "train a dense model"),
                        ("eval", "evaluate a saved checkpoint"),
                        ("bench", "benchmark a saved checkpoint")):
        p = sub.add_parser(name, help=help_)
        p.add_argument("--model", required=True, choices=["mlp", "cnn", "gcn"])
        p.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=0)
        p.add_argument("--run-id", default=None)
        # overrides (tests only)
        p.add_argument("--lr", type=float, default=None)
        p.add_argument("--weight-decay", type=float, default=None)
        p.add_argument("--batch-size", type=int, default=None)
        p.add_argument("--epochs", type=int, default=None)
        p.add_argument("--patience", type=int, default=None)

    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    set_threads()

    if args.cmd == "make-splits":
        args.fn()
        return 0

    cfg = load_config(args.model)
    cfg = _apply_overrides(cfg, args)

    if args.cmd == "train":
        from .training import train
        rec = train(args.model, cfg, seed=args.seed, run_id=args.run_id)
        print(f"run_id={rec['run_id']} best_epoch={rec['best_epoch']} "
              f"val_acc={rec['val_acc']:.4f} test_acc={rec['test_acc']:.4f} "
              f"epochs={rec['train_epochs']} wall={rec['wall_time_s']}s")
    elif args.cmd == "eval":
        from .evaln import eval as do_eval
        rec = do_eval(args.model, seed=args.seed)
        print(f"run_id={rec['run_id']} val_acc={rec['val_acc']:.4f} test_acc={rec['test_acc']:.4f}")
    elif args.cmd == "bench":
        from .bench import bench
        rec = bench(args.model, seed=args.seed)
        lat = rec["latency"]
        print(f"run_id={rec['run_id']} latency={lat} peak_rss={rec['peak_rss_bytes']}B")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

    """run_ids of all earlier successful `bench` records for this (arch, seed), in
    file order. Used to fill `supersedes` on a corrected re-bench. The log is
    append-only: earlier lines are never edited or deleted."""
    out = []

                out.append(r["run_id"])

"""Frozen latency protocol (Part A.1) + analytical MAC estimates.

Latency: torch.inference_mode(), model in eval(). 20 warm-up and 200 timed
iterations, time.perf_counter_ns. Report median and IQR (q3 - q1).
The fixed benchmark input is the first 256 TEST images (inputs only, saved once
to a small file, results/bench/fmnist_bench_input.pt) — NOT training images.
Batch sizes 1 and 256 for Fashion-MNIST; one full-graph forward for Cora.

Memory: the RSS subprocess does not load the 55k training tensor. It loads the
small fixed bench input and the checkpoint, and reports
rss_before_model_bytes (after imports + input load), peak_rss_bytes and
model_rss_delta_bytes = peak - before.

MAC counting (computed from the ACTUAL model's layer shapes — works for any
Linear / Conv2d / GCNConv sizes; nothing is hard-coded). We trace one forward
pass with hooks, and for every weight-bearing module (Linear, Conv2d, GCNConv)
count the MACs its weight performs per single sample:

- Linear(in, out):   each weight element multiplies one input per token;
  MACs = numel(W) * tokens (tokens = 1 here, i.e. per image / per node).
- Conv2d(cin, cout, k): each weight element is applied at every output-pixel
  position; MACs = numel(W) * H_out * W_out per image.
- GCNConv(in, out):   GCNConv computes X @ W ONCE per node (not per edge) and
  then aggregates over the augmented adjacency A' = A + I (self-loops). Per
  layer:
      projection   = N * in * out       (the dense-X weight product)
      aggregation  = (E + N) * out      (weighted sum over the E+N A' entries)
  where N = node count, E = directed edges (A' adds N self-loops).
  The degree-normalization factors D^{1/2} are elementwise scales and add
  ~2 * out * (E+N) multiplications; these are reported separately under
  `gcn_norm_macs` and are NOT part of est_macs.

Two MAC fields are emitted for every model:
- est_macs          : MACs assuming ALL weights are nonzero (dense convention).
                      For GCN this is the dense-X total above.
- est_macs_nonzero  : the same count but only for weight elements that are
                      actually nonzero in the loaded checkpoint (this is what
                      matters once Part B makes the model physically sparse).
GCN additionally reports:
- est_macs_sparse_input : est_macs with the layer-1 projection counted as
                      nnz(X)*out instead of N*in*out, because Cora's features
                      are ~1.3% dense (sparse-input convention).

For the dense seed-0 baselines every weight is nonzero, so
est_macs == est_macs_nonzero.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import statistics
import subprocess
import sys
import time

import numpy as np
import torch
import torch.nn as nn

from .data import fmnist_split_tensors, load_cora
from .evaln import load_checkpoint
from .models import compact_export_bytes, count_params, dense_bytes, raw_tensor_bytes
from .util import (
    BENCH_DIR,
    RUNS_JSONL,
    ROOT,
    base_record,
    prior_bench_run_ids,
    run_wall_timer,
    set_threads,
    write_run_record,
)

WARMUP = 20
TIMED = 200
BATCH_SIZES = [1, 256]
FMNIST_BENCH_INPUT = BENCH_DIR / "fmnist_bench_input.pt"
CORAL_BENCH_INPUT = BENCH_DIR / "cora_bench_input.pt"


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Fixed benchmark inputs (inputs only). Saved once, reused by the main process
# and the RSS subprocess so neither ever loads the 55k training tensor.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _ensure_fmnist_bench_input() -> torch.Tensor:
    """First 256 TEST images, inputs only (no labels). Saved once."""
    if FMNIST_BENCH_INPUT.exists():
        return torch.load(FMNIST_BENCH_INPUT, map_location="cpu", weights_only=True)
    _, _, _, _, te_x, _, _, _ = fmnist_split_tensors()
    BENCH_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    torch.save(te_x[:256].contiguous(), FMNIST_BENCH_INPUT)
    return torch.load(FMNIST_BENCH_INPUT, map_location="cpu", weights_only=True)


def _ensure_cora_bench_input() -> dict:
    """Full-graph Cora features + edge_index (inputs only). Saved once."""
    if CORAL_BENCH_INPUT.exists():
        return torch.load(CORAL_BENCH_INPUT, map_location="cpu", weights_only=False)
    data = load_cora()
    BENCH_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    payload = {"x": data.x.contiguous(), "edge_index": data.edge_index.contiguous()}
    torch.save(payload, CORAL_BENCH_INPUT)
    return torch.load(CORAL_BENCH_INPUT, map_location="cpu", weights_only=False)


def load_bench_input(architecture: str):
    """Return the fixed benchmark input: (x, edge_index). edge_index is None for
    fmnist; x is the (256,1,28,28) test-image batch for fmnist and the full
    (N,in) Cora feature matrix for gcn."""
    if architecture == "gcn":
        d = _ensure_cora_bench_input()
        return d["x"], d["edge_index"]
    return _ensure_fmnist_bench_input(), None


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# MAC estimation from actual layer shapes (no hard-coded numbers).
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _mac_entries(model, x, edge_index=None):
    """Run one forward pass, recording (weight numel, weight nnz, out_ch,
    tokens) for each Linear / Conv2d / GCNConv in forward order."""
    from torch_geometric.nn import GCNConv

    model.eval()
    entries = []
    hooks = []
    for name, mod in model.named_modules():
        if isinstance(mod, (nn.Linear, nn.Conv2d)) or type(mod).__name__ == "GCNConv":
            def _hook(m, inp, out, _mod=mod, _name=name):
                w = _mod.weight
                tokens = int(out.numel()) // int(out.shape[-1])
                entries.append({
                    "name": _name,
                    "type": type(_mod).__name__,
                    "numel": int(w.numel()),
                    "nnz": int(w.count_nonzero()),
                    "out_ch": int(out.shape[-1]),
                    "tokens": tokens,
                })
            hooks.append(mod.register_forward_hook(_hook))
    try:
        with torch.inference_mode():
            if edge_index is not None:
                model(x, edge_index)
            else:
                model(x)
    finally:
        for h in hooks:
            h.remove()
    return entries


def estimate_macs(model, x, edge_index=None, x_nnz: int | None = None) -> dict:
    """Analytical MAC estimate computed from the model's actual layer shapes.

    Returns dict with est_macs, est_macs_nonzero, gcn_norm_macs and
    est_macs_sparse_input (GCN only, else None).
    """
    entries = _mac_entries(model, x, edge_index)

    is_gcn = edge_index is not None
    if is_gcn:
        N = int(x.shape[0])
        E = int(edge_index.shape[1])          # directed edges (no self-loops yet)
        E_plus_N = E + N                      # A' = A + I
        norm_macs = 0
    else:
        N = E_plus_N = None
        norm_macs = 0

    est = 0
    est_nz = 0
    est_sparse = est
    first_gcn_done = False
    for e in entries:
        if e["type"] == "GCNConv":
            proj = e["numel"] * e["tokens"]              # N*in*out (dense-X)
            proj_nz = e["nnz"] * e["tokens"]             # nonzero weights only
            agg = E_plus_N * e["out_ch"]
            est += proj + agg
            est_nz += proj_nz + agg
            if not first_gcn_done and x_nnz is not None:
                est_sparse = est - proj + (x_nnz * e["out_ch"])
                first_gcn_done = True
            norm_macs += 2 * e["out_ch"] * E_plus_N
        else:  # Linear / Conv2d
            est += e["numel"] * e["tokens"]
            est_nz += e["nnz"] * e["tokens"]

    return {
        "est_macs": est,
        "est_macs_nonzero": est_nz,
        "est_macs_sparse_input": (est_sparse if is_gcn else None),
        "gcn_norm_macs": norm_macs,
    }


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Timing (frozen protocol) and peak-RSS subprocess.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def _time_batch(model, x, batch_size: int) -> dict:
    """Frozen protocol: inference_mode, eval(), 20 warm-up / 200 timed iterations.
    A pre-allocated (batch_size, ...) view of the fixed bench input is used each
    iteration so the timed region is the model forward pass only."""
    model.eval()
    with torch.inference_mode():
        xb = x[:batch_size] if len(x) >= batch_size else x
        for _ in range(WARMUP):
            model(xb)
        ns = []
        for _ in range(TIMED):
            t0 = time.perf_counter_ns()
            model(xb)
            ns.append(time.perf_counter_ns() - t0)
    ns = np.asarray(ns, dtype=np.float64) / 1e6
    q1, q2, q3 = np.percentile(ns, [25, 50, 75])
    return {"median_ms": float(q2), "iqr_ms": float(q3 - q1)}


def _bench_peak_rss(architecture: str, seed: int) -> dict:
    """RSS measured in a fresh subprocess that (1) imports + loads the small
    fixed bench input, (2) records rss_before_model_bytes, (3) loads the
    checkpoint and runs a few forwards, recording peak_rss_bytes. Returns
    (rss_before, peak)."""
    code = f"""
import psutil, sys
import torch
from lab3.util import set_threads
from lab3.bench import load_bench_input
from lab3.evaln import load_checkpoint
set_threads()
x, ei = load_bench_input("{architecture}")
proc = psutil.Process()
before = proc.memory_info().rss
m, _ = load_checkpoint("{architecture}", {seed})
m.eval()
peak = before
with torch.inference_mode():
    for _ in range(5):
        if "{architecture}" == "gcn":
            m(x, ei)
        else:
            m(x[:256])
        peak = max(peak, proc.memory_info().rss)
print(json.dumps({{"before": int(before), "peak": int(peak)}}))
"""
    proc = subprocess.run(
        [sys.executable, "-c", code],
        capture_output=True, text=True, check=True, cwd=str(ROOT),
        env={**os.environ, "PYTHONPATH": str(ROOT / "code")},
    )
    out = json.loads(proc.stdout.strip().splitlines()[-1])
    return out


def bench(architecture: str, seed: int = 0) -> dict:
    set_threads()
    t0 = time.perf_counter()
    rec = base_record(architecture, command="bench")
    rec["seed"] = seed
    try:
        model, meta = load_checkpoint(architecture, seed)
        # Linkage: parent run is the training run that produced this checkpoint.
        rec["parent_run_id"] = meta.get("run_id")
        rec["supersedes"] = prior_bench_run_ids(architecture, seed)

        rec["total_params"] = count_params(model)
        rec["nonzero_params"] = count_params(model)
        rec["dense_bytes"] = dense_bytes(model)
        rec["raw_tensor_bytes"] = raw_tensor_bytes(model)
        # compressed_bytes is the Part B 'compact export' field; null for dense.
        rec["compressed_bytes"] = None
        rec["best_epoch"] = meta.get("best_epoch")
        rec["val_acc"] = meta.get("val_acc")

        x, ei = load_bench_input(architecture)
        model.eval()

        if architecture == "gcn":
            with torch.inference_mode():
                for _ in range(WARMUP):
                    model(x, ei)
                ns = []
                for _ in range(TIMED):
                    t_start = time.perf_counter_ns()
                    model(x, ei)
                    ns.append(time.perf_counter_ns() - t_start)
            ns = np.asarray(ns, dtype=np.float64) / 1e6
            q1, q2, q3 = np.percentile(ns, [25, 50, 75])
            rec["latency"] = {
                "full_graph": {
                    "median_ms": float(q2),
                    "iqr_ms": float(q3 - q1),
                    "warmup": WARMUP,
                    "iters": TIMED,
                    "threads": torch.get_num_threads(),
                    "batch_size": "full_graph",
                }
            }
            macs = estimate_macs(model, x, ei, x_nnz=int(x.count_nonzero()))
        else:
            lat = {}
            for bs in BATCH_SIZES:
                lat[f"batch_{bs}"] = _time_batch(model, x, bs)
                lat[f"batch_{bs}"].update({"warmup": WARMUP, "iters": TIMED,
                                           "threads": torch.get_num_threads(),
                                           "batch_size": bs})
            rec["latency"] = lat
            macs = estimate_macs(model, x[:1], None)

        rec["est_macs"] = macs["est_macs"]
        rec["est_macs_nonzero"] = macs["est_macs_nonzero"]
        rec["est_macs_sparse_input"] = macs["est_macs_sparse_input"]
        rec["gcn_norm_macs"] = macs["gcn_norm_macs"]

        rss = _bench_peak_rss(architecture, seed)
        rec["rss_before_model_bytes"] = rss["before"]
        rec["peak_rss_bytes"] = rss["peak"]
        rec["model_rss_delta_bytes"] = rss["peak"] - rss["before"]

        rec = run_wall_timer(rec, t0)
        write_run_record(rec)
        return rec
    except Exception as e:
        rec = run_wall_timer(rec, t0)
        rec["status"] = "failed"
        rec["reason"] = f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"
        write_run_record(rec)
        raise

"""Test (c): the REAL lab3 evaluation and bench timing code never update
weights. We load the actual saved seed-0 checkpoint, snapshot its
state_dict (bit-exact), requires_grad flags and grad fields, then call the
genuine ``lab3.evaln.eval`` and ``lab3.bench.bench`` functions on it and assert
the checkpoint parameters are bit-identical with grad still None. Covers all
three architectures."""
import pytest
import torch
import torch.nn as nn

from lab3.bench import bench
from lab3.data import fmnist_split_tensors, load_cora
from lab3.evaln import eval as do_eval, load_checkpoint
from lab3.models import build_model
from lab3.util import set_threads
from test_splits import _make_splits_once

ARCHS = ("mlp", "cnn", "gcn")


def _snapshot(model: nn.Module) -> dict:
    """Bit-exact parameter bytes plus requires_grad flags and grad fields."""
    snap = {
        "params": {k: v.view(torch.uint8).clone()
                   for k, v in model.state_dict().items()},
        "requires_grad": {n: bool(p.requires_grad)
                          for n, p in model.named_parameters()},
        "grad": {n: (None if p.grad is None else p.grad.view(torch.uint8).clone())
                 for n, p in model.named_parameters()},
    }
    return snap


def _assert_unchanged(before: dict, model: nn.Module) -> None:
    after_sd = model.state_dict()
    assert set(before["params"]) == set(after_sd), "state_dict keys changed"
    for k, b in before["params"].items():
        a = after_sd[k]
        assert a.dtype == b.view(dtype=a.dtype).dtype
        assert torch.equal(b, a.view(torch.uint8)), f"tensor {k} changed bytes"
    for n, p in model.named_parameters():
        assert bool(p.requires_grad) == before["requires_grad"][n], \
            f"requires_grad changed for {n}"
        gb = before["grad"][n]
        ga = p.grad
        if gb is None:
            assert ga is None, f"grad materialized for {n}"
        else:
            assert ga is not None
            assert torch.equal(gb, ga.view(torch.uint8)), f"grad changed for {n}"


@pytest.mark.parametrize("arch", ARCHS)
def test_real_eval_never_updates(arch):
    """The real lab3.evaln.eval on the loaded checkpoint leaves weights bit-identical
    and grad/requires_grad untouched."""
    set_threads()
    _make_splits_once()
    # Preload data so eval does the same work as the production call.
    if arch == "gcn":
        load_cora()
    else:
        fmnist_split_tensors()
    model, _ = load_checkpoint(arch, seed=0)
    before = _snapshot(model)
    do_eval(arch, seed=0)  # real evaluation function; appends a run record
    _assert_unchanged(before, model)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("arch", ARCHS)
def test_real_bench_never_updates(arch):
    """The real lab3.bench.bench timing/protocol on the loaded checkpoint leaves
    weights bit-identical and grad/requires_grad untouched."""
    set_threads()
    _make_splits_once()
    model, _ = load_checkpoint(arch, seed=0)
    before = _snapshot(model)
    bench(arch, seed=0)  # real bench function; appends a run record
    _assert_unchanged(before, model)

# Lab 3 `results/runs.jsonl` record schema

Every command (`train`, `eval`, `bench`) appends exactly one JSON object per
attempted run to `results/runs.jsonl` (append-only: lines are never edited or
deleted; a corrected re-bench adds a new line whose `supersedes` lists the
earlier, now-incorrect run_ids). This file documents the fields.

## Identity / linkage

| field | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `run_id` | str | Unique id for this record: `<arch>-<method>-<UTC timestamp>-<shortuuid>`. |
| `status` | str | `"ok"` or `"failed"`. |
| `reason` | str/null | Failure reason when `status == "failed"`. |
| `part` | str | `"A"` (dense reference). |
| `architecture` | str | `mlp` / `cnn` / `gcn`. |
| `method` | str | `"dense"` for the Part A baseline. |
| `seed` | int | Random seed. |
| `command` | str | `train` / `eval` / `bench`. |
| `parent_run_id` | str/null | For `bench` (and `eval`), the `run_id` of the **training run** that produced the checkpoint being benchmarked. Carried from the checkpoint metadata `run_id`. |
| `supersedes` | list[str] | For a corrected re-bench: the `run_id`s of the earlier bench records for the same (architecture, seed) that are now known to be incorrect (e.g. A1's wrong MAC/byte figures). The old lines remain in the log untouched. |

## Training / selection

| field | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `train_epochs` | int/null | Epochs actually run (may stop early). |
| `finetune_epochs` | int | 0 in Part A. |
| `best_epoch` | int/null | Epoch of the validation-selected checkpoint. |
| `val_acc`, `val_loss` | float/null | Validation accuracy / loss. |
| `test_acc` | float/null | Test accuracy (evaluated only on the selected checkpoint). |

## Size

| field | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `total_params` | int | `sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters())`. |
| `nonzero_params` | int | Number of nonzero weight/param elements. For the dense baseline this equals `total_params`; Part B arms report the physically sparse count. |
| `dense_bytes` | int | **Actual on-disk size** (bytes) of a `torch.save(state_dict)` file — the bare state dict (no metadata) written to a temp file, read with `os.path.getsize`. Includes the PyTorch zip/pickle container overhead, so it is slightly larger than `raw_tensor_bytes`. |
| `raw_tensor_bytes` | int | `sum(t.numel() * t.element_size())` over every state_dict tensor — pure payload bytes, no container overhead. |
| `compressed_bytes` | int/null | Size (bytes) of the `dense_bytes` state_dict file gzipped at level 9. This is the "compact export" figure used by Part B. **Null for the dense Part A baseline** (dense has no compressed export). |

## Compute (MAC estimates)

Computed from the actual model's layer shapes (works for any
Linear/Conv2d/GCNConv sizes), not hard-coded. Per single sample (per image /
per node for fmnist-MLP/CNN; full graph for GCN).

| field | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `est_macs` | int | Total forward MACs assuming **all weights are nonzero** (dense convention). |
| `est_macs_nonzero` | int | Same count but only over weight elements that are **actually nonzero** in the loaded checkpoint. Equals `est_macs` for the dense baseline; smaller once Part B prunes weights. |
| `est_macs_sparse_input` | int/null | GCN only: `est_macs` with the layer-1 projection counted as `nnz(X) * out` instead of `N * in * out`, because Cora's node features are ~1.3% dense (sparse-input convention). Null for MLP/CNN. |
| `gcn_norm_macs` | int/null | GCN only: the degree-normalization (D^{1/2}) elementwise scaling multiplications, `2 * out * (E + N)` per GCNConv layer, reported **separately** and excluded from `est_macs`. Null for MLP/CNN. |

### MAC conventions

- **Linear(in, out):** `in * out` per token (1 per image / per node). Bias excluded.
- **Conv2d(cin, cout, k, padding):** `cin * cout * k^2 * H_out * W_out` per image
  (`H_out`/`W_out` are the actual output feature-map dims after padding). MaxPool/ReLU contribute 0.
- **GCNConv(in, out)** (torch_geometric, self-loops added): the weight is applied **once per
  node** (`X @ W`), not per edge. Per layer:
  - projection = `N * in * out` (dense-X weight product),
  - aggregation = `(E + N) * out` (weighted sum over the E directed edges plus N self-loops).
  - `est_macs` = sum over layers of (projection + aggregation); normalization scales go in `gcn_norm_macs`.
  - `est_macs_sparse_input` = `est_macs` but with the layer-1 projection replaced by `nnz(X) * out`.
  - For Cora: N = 2,708, E = 10,556, in1 = 1,433, out1 = 16, in2 = 16, out2 = 7 →
    `est_macs` ≈ 6.27e7, `est_macs_nonzero` = `est_macs` (dense),
    `est_macs_sparse_input` ≈ 1.0e6.

### Dense seed-0 reference values

- MLP: `est_macs` = 234,752 per image.
- CNN: `est_macs` = 1,697,280 per image (conv2 output is 10×10: 28 → conv1 pad2 → 28 →
  pool → 14 → conv2 5×5 no pad → 10 → pool → 5).

## Memory

Measured in a fresh subprocess that (1) imports torch + loads the **small fixed
benchmark input** (never the 55k training tensor), records `rss_before_model_bytes`,
(2) loads the checkpoint and runs a few forwards, recording the peak.

| field | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `rss_before_model_bytes` | int | RSS after imports + benchmark-input load, **before** loading the model. |
| `peak_rss_bytes` | int | Peak RSS observed while loading the model and running forwards. |
| `model_rss_delta_bytes` | int | `peak_rss_bytes - rss_before_model_bytes` — the memory attributable to the model + activations. |

## Latency

Frozen protocol: `torch.inference_mode()`, `model.eval()`, 20 warm-up + 200 timed
iterations, `time.perf_counter_ns`, median and IQR reported. Inputs are the fixed
**benchmark batch** (first 256 TEST images, inputs only) — not training images.

`latency` is a dict keyed by `batch_1` / `batch_256` (fmnist) or `full_graph` (gcn),
each with: `median_ms`, `iqr_ms`, `warmup`, `iters`, `threads`, `batch_size`.

## Provenance

| field | type | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `wall_time_s` | float | Wall-clock seconds for the command. |
| `code_hash` | str | SHA-256 over all files under `code/` (git-free). |
| `versions` | dict | python / torch / numpy / platform versions. |
| `timestamp` | str | ISO-8601 UTC creation time. |
| `target_sparsity`, `achieved_sparsity`, `stored_precision`, `compute_precision`, `accumulator_precision` | — | 0.0 / "fp32" for the dense baseline. |

## Fixed benchmark input

`results/bench/fmnist_bench_input.pt` = first 256 TEST Fashion-MNIST images,
inputs only (no labels), saved once. `results/bench/cora_bench_input.pt` = full-graph
Cora features + edge_index. These are the latency/RSS inputs and are independent of
the 55k training tensor.

  via `os.path.getsize`; `raw_tensor_bytes` = `sum(numel × element_size)`; the
  difference is the PyTorch zip/pickle container overhead. `compressed_bytes`

- MACs computed from the actual layer shapes. Dense baselines have every weight
  nonzero, so `est_macs == est_macs_nonzero` here.
  - MLP: 784·256 + 256·128 + 128·10 = **234,752** per image.
  - CNN: 1·16·25·28·28 + 16·32·25·10·10 + 800·128 + 128·10 = **1,697,280** per image

- Memory (RSS) measured in a fresh subprocess that loads the small fixed benchmark

- Linkage: each bench record carries `parent_run_id` (the training run whose
